Theme

School & learning

graduate verb and noun

finish a university degree; one who has

also graduates, graduated, graduation, university graduate, college graduate, graduate from university

modern

M-O s.v. graduate vb. (lauream vel gradum acadēmicum adipīscī)
Traupman 29, 323 (gradūs suscipiō)

gradum acadēmicum adipīscor

phrase: adipīscor, adipīscī, adeptus sum, deponent

to graduate, to take a degree

A modern thing in classical words. A graduate is quī gradum acadēmicum adeptus est (M-O s.v. graduate subst.).

Other words

  • laureā dōnor — to graduate (to be given the laurel)

    phrase: passive of dōnō with the ablative · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. graduate vb., citing Vives (1540)

    After the laurel of the old degree ceremonies.

  • diplōma adipīscor — to graduate (to get one’s diploma)

    phrase · also used · modern · Traupman 323

    Classically a diplōma is an official letter of recommendation or a pass for the public post (Cic.); the degree certificate is modern.

  • graduātus, graduātī m. — a graduate; a woman is graduāta

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 323

    Not in Lewis & Short; formed on medieval gradus, an academic degree.

See also university, student, academic.

SourcesLewis & Short: adipiscor · Lewis & Short: laurea · Lewis & Short: diploma
